title: Conditional shell-tail composition for direct D and modular derivative
question: If reference and dual cutoff tails decay as K_i/s^2 along R=s^5, L=s^2, does a uniform Duhamel integrand bound imply a vanishing combined squared D and delta-D tail?
method: Rewrite the EXP-001111/112 safe polynomial tail on the exact fifth-power shell subsequence R=s^5, L=s^2 as K_i/s^2.
Assume, without proving for Q3, squared direct-D and delta-D Duhamel integrands bounded by a_0^2 K_0/s^2 and a_1^2 K_1/s^2 uniformly over time.
Apply the scalar Cauchy-Schwarz Duhamel composition and independently recompute the resulting coefficient and exact shell fixtures.
Compile Lean R285 for the inverse-square limit and rational coefficient only.
finding: Primary 17/17, independent 11/11, integrated 11/11, and Lean R285 compile PASS. With K_0=K_1=38880, a_0=1/2, a_1=3/4 and t=1/5, the combined squared bound is (6318/5)/L on L=s^2. The exact rows for (R,L)=(1,1),(32,4),(3125,25) are 6318/5, 3159/10 and 6318/125, respectively, and the Lean inverse-square theorem gives the zero limit along s to infinity.

It closes only a conditional interface: the actual Q3 dual modular tail and both common-core Duhamel integrand bounds are not supplied, so direct D/delta-D Cauchy and common-alpha remain open.
